## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
The package contains a dependency management file or installation script (e.g. renv.lock or groundhog in R, a setup.do in Stata) that installs all required packages/libraries with their exact versions and runs successfully, or the README lists all packages/software used with their exact versions, and these can be successfully installed at the point of reproduction.

[Supported by: Installer/lock file: [#19](../../sources.qmd#p19 "The ReproRubric: evaluation criteria for the reproducibility of computational analyses") 'installed/updated by a script', [#108](../../sources.qmd#p108 "Checklists for computational reproducibility in social sciences: insights from literature and survey evaluation") requirements.txt, [#120](../../sources.qmd#p120 "Reproducibility spectrum for applied social sciences: conceptual taxonomy and recommended tools") renv/conda/pip, [#134](../../sources.qmd#p134 "PaperRepro: automated computational reproducibility assessment for social science papers") single installation script, [#79](../../sources.qmd#p79 "A review of containerization for interactive and reproducible analysis") renv/checkpoint/groundhog. Listing with versions: [#95](../../sources.qmd#p95 "Computational reproducibility in finance: evidence from 1,000 tests") R3, [#117](../../sources.qmd#p117 "Computational reproducibility of R code supplements on OSF"), [#40](../../sources.qmd#p40 "The role of containers in reproducibility"), [#38](../../sources.qmd#p38 "Ten simple rules for writing dockerfiles for reproducible data science") pin versions, [#70](../../sources.qmd#p70 "The Stark realities of reproducible statistically orientated sociological research: Some newer rules of the sociological method"), [#48](../../sources.qmd#p48 "Challenges of curating for reproducible and FAIR research output"), [#57](../../sources.qmd#p57 "Principles for data analysis workflows"), [#7](../../sources.qmd#p7 "Tools and techniques for computational reproducibility").]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
A dependency management file, installation script, or README list of dependencies is available, but it is incomplete (some packages or their versions are missing) or it cannot be successfully executed/installed at the point of reproduction (e.g. a package has been removed from its repository).

[Supported by: [#44](../../sources.qmd#p44 "Active maintenance: a proposal for the long-term computational reproducibility of scientific results") packages removed from CRAN, [#103](../../sources.qmd#p103 "The Challenges of Replicating Volatile Platform-Data Studies: Replicating Schatto-Eckrodt et al. (2020)") deprecated packages, [#61](../../sources.qmd#p61 "A collaborative semantic-based provenance management platform for reproducibility") version change breaks code, [#143](../../sources.qmd#p143 "What is Computational Reproducibility?").]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
No dependency management file, installation script, or README information on dependencies is available.

[Supported by: [#10](../../sources.qmd#p10 "Sustainable computational science: the ReScience initiative") 'undocumented dependencies', [#73](../../sources.qmd#p73 "A backend platform for supporting the reproducibility of computational experiments") 'no information about how to install the project', [#77](../../sources.qmd#p77 "Report of the AEA data editor") manifest files 'remain rare'.]{.source-note}
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never. If no add-on packages are used, met when the README says so.
:::

> "One of the major challenges in computational reproducibility and reuse is capturing code dependencies necessary for its execution. These dependencies are currently not captured for much of the published research code, which is one of the major causes of non-reproducibility reported across fields." (p. 5) and "One of the best reproducibility practices is to test research code in a clean environment before publishing it or sharing it online. Doing that helps the researcher (or code depositor) identify common errors such as fixed file paths, missing dependencies, and missing files." (p. 5)

*Note:* The RE3 platform automates dependency installation via Docker/Conda
